idiom_name: protocol CustomerDao over GRDB's DatabaseQueue (SwiftData/Core Data as the framework alternative)
implementation_notes: Swift expresses the DAO as a protocol plus one implementation per store: GRDB is the common choice for SQL stores (DatabaseQueue/DatabasePool with read/write closures and FetchableRecord/PersistableRecord models), while SwiftData supplies a framework-level gateway in which @Model classes are managed by a ModelContext that performs inserts, fetches and saves. What replaces the classic structure is the protocol plus value semantics: implementations are structs/actors, results are Codable structs, and failures are thrown typed errors, so no store handle appears in the interface. Keep a hand-written protocol DAO when the app talks to several stores or an existing SQLite schema; using SwiftData directly is simpler when there is only one model graph.
pitfalls: DatabaseQueue serialises access from a single thread: concurrent reads need DatabasePool, and hammering a queue from many threads produces contention rather than parallelism.
Core Data and SwiftData objects are context/actor-bound: returning an NSManagedObject or @Model instance from a DAO crosses isolation boundaries, so map to value types at the boundary.
GRDB and Core Data throw store-specific errors; letting them escape the protocol leaks the persistence layer, so declare the DAO's own error type and translate inside the implementation.
